payload.recallText: I grew up in providence, Rhode Island, where  my family was obsessed with the Kennedy family. One thanksgiving, my dad told me never to be ashamed to cry for JFK. Every summer, my aunts took us to Hyannis and spent all day spying on the Kennedys with binoculars. One day, my cousins and I drifted out to sea in a small boat and were rescued by David and Michael Kennedy. Our aunts were more upset that the Kennedys had to save us than that we almost drowned, so we were punished to stay on the beach. Later, while playing in shallow water, I accidentally kicked my uncle Al and his fake eye popped out and sank. We searched until it was found and he put it back in. At the end, I realized the Kennedy boys had seen the whole incident.
